whatIsDash.question: What is Dash?
whatIsDash.answer: Dash is an open-source cryptocurrency that was forked from Bitcoin in January 2014. The name "Dash" comes from "Digital Cash." It focuses on being a fast, cheap global payments network with features like InstantSend (transactions confirm in 1-2 seconds), optional privacy through PrivateSend, and extremely low fees (typically $0.01-$0.02 per transaction).

whoInvented.question: Who invented Dash?
whoInvented.answer: Based on the Bitcoin project, Dash was launched on January 18, 2014 by founder Evan Duffield. The first few years of development saw Dash develop a focus on speed and fungibility, making it an excellent and practical alternative to cash, both online and at the point of sale in shops and restaurants.

whatUsedFor.question: What is Dash used for?
whatUsedFor.answer: Dash is used for fast, private, and low-cost payments both online and at physical point-of-sale locations. It's designed to work like digital cash — transactions confirm in seconds and can be immediately spent by the recipient. Dash is also used for cross-border payments, remittances, and as a store of value in regions with unstable local currencies.

whoControls.question: Who controls Dash?
whoControls.answer: No single entity controls Dash. It operates as one of the world's oldest Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAO). Decisions are made collectively by masternode operators who vote on proposals for network changes, marketing, and development. The network self-funds through a treasury system that allocates 10% of block rewards to approved projects.

wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.content: A digital wallet is a software program or physical device that stores your cryptocurrency keys and allows you to send and receive digital currency.

p2p.title: P2P
p2p.content: Peer-to-peer (P2P) refers to the direct exchange of cryptocurrency between individuals without an intermediary, like a bank or centralized exchange.

publicAddress.title: Public Address
publicAddress.content: A public address is a cryptographic hash of a public key, serving as an identifier that can be shared to receive cryptocurrency transactions.

exchange.title: [CryptoCurrency] Exchange
exchange.content: A cryptocurrency exchange is an online platform where you can buy, sell, and trade cryptocurrencies using fiat money or other digital currencies.

qrCode.title: QR Code
qrCode.content: A Quick Response code that contains a wallet address and can optionally include a payment amount, making cryptocurrency transactions quick and easy.

block1.title: Lower Transaction Fees
block1.description: At the top of the list is lower transaction fees. The costs incurred from traditional payment system fees can add up. These costs can be significantly reduced by accepting a cryptocurrency like Dash. <highlight>Credit card processing fees can cost a business between 1.5% to 3.5% of each transaction's total. Transactions that are considered "high-risk" may be hit with even higher rates per transaction</highlight> (ie: card not present, gambling, cannabis, etc.). With crypto, depending on the coin, the same costs can be reduced down to mere cents -- regardless of merchant category.

block2.title: No Chargebacks
block2.description: Accepting crypto payments also means no chargebacks, which can be incredibly costly to businesses – both in regard to the monetary value and time. <highlight>A chargeback can cost your business the price of the item being disputed, as well as the chargeback fees incurred, and the time needed to dispute fraudulent chargebacks.</highlight> No centralized institution can reverse the crypto payments made to your business. Your business can choose to set up refund policies on your own terms.

transactions.quote: With Dash, accepting crypto payments is as <bold>easy as spending your profit.</bold>

createDashpay.title: How to Create a Dashpay
createDashpay.content: Download the DashPay app from the official app stores (Google Play Store or Apple App Store). Check the developer name matches 'Dash Core Group' and verify the app has significant download numbers and positive reviews. Follow the in-app setup wizard to create your wallet.

addingFunds.title: Adding funds to Dashpay
addingFunds.content: Once you've installed DashPay, you can add funds by receiving Dash from another wallet, purchasing Dash through a supported exchange, or having someone send Dash to your wallet address or DashPay username.

assistance.title: Need Assistance?
assistance.content: If you need help setting up your wallet, visit the Dash support page or join the Dash Discord community where helpful volunteers can assist you with any questions.

sendReceive.title:
How to Send &
Receive Dash
sendReceive.paragraph1: The easiest way to receive Dash as a payment from your customers is by showing them a QR code that they can scan. Both your public address and the associated QR code can be seen/copied by clicking the Receive button in the DashPay app. If you buy Dash at an exchange that is not already integrated with your DashPay app, you just need to know your public address to transfer your digital cash to the app.
sendReceive.paragraph2: There are a few ways to send Dash from your DashPay, the easiest way is by scanning a QR code. This is done by clicking the Scan to Send button in the app.

createAccount.title: Create an Account on a Reputable Crypto/Fiat exchange
createAccount.content: Sign up on a regulated and well-known exchange such as Kraken, Binance, Coinbase, or Uphold. You'll need to complete identity verification (KYC) which typically requires a government-issued ID and proof of address.

howExchangesWork.title: How Exchanges Work
howExchangesWork.content: Crypto exchanges operate similarly to stock exchanges. You deposit fiat currency (USD, EUR, etc.), place buy orders for Dash at market or limit prices, and the exchange matches your order with a seller. Once purchased, Dash appears in your exchange wallet.

withdrawalFreezes.title: Withdrawal Freezes
withdrawalFreezes.content: Many exchanges impose a temporary withdrawal hold on new accounts or after large deposits. This is typically 24-72 hours but can vary. Plan ahead to ensure you have access to your Dash when you need it.

whereDoesItGo.title: Where Does My Dash Go After I Purchase on an Exchange
whereDoesItGo.content: After purchasing, your Dash sits in your exchange wallet. For maximum security, transfer it to your personal wallet (like DashPay) where you control the private keys. Simply copy your wallet address and initiate a withdrawal from the exchange.

posGuide.posTitle:
How to Choose
a POS System
posGuide.posDescription: If you've decided that utilizing a POS will benefit your processes, finding a system that meets the requirements and budget of your business is essential. Here are several items to consider:
posGuide.posAnswer: A POS system comes with many benefits, like invoicing, inventory management, etc. Depending on the POS system you select, you may have the option to install a physical payment terminal (much like the chip/card reader for credit card transactions), create invoices, receipts, generate transaction history and reports, and even automatically convert crypto to fiat (or vice versa).
posGuide.description1: While you can simply use a Dash wallet, at no cost, it may be useful to utilize a Point of Sale system.
posGuide.description2: A crypto Point of Sale (POS) system is similar to traditional POS systems utilized for cash and credit card transactions but also adds the ability to receive payments in one or more cryptocurrencies.

posAccordion.subtitle: Here are several items to consider:
posAccordion.title: How to Choose a POS System

first.title: What is a POS System?
first.content: A Point of Sale system is hardware and/or software that processes customer payments at the time of purchase. For crypto, this means generating QR codes, detecting incoming payments, and confirming transactions in real-time.

cost.title: Consider the Cost
cost.content: POS costs vary widely — from free software-only solutions to dedicated hardware terminals costing hundreds of dollars. Consider setup fees, monthly subscriptions, per-transaction fees, and any hardware purchases required.

tools.title: What Tools Do You Need?
tools.content: Consider whether you need physical hardware (a terminal), a mobile app, eCommerce integration, invoicing capabilities, automatic fiat conversion, and multi-coin support. Match the POS features to your business requirements.

setup.title: How Straightforward is The Setup Process?
setup.content: Some POS systems require technical knowledge to set up, while others offer plug-and-play simplicity. Consider your technical comfort level and whether the provider offers setup assistance and ongoing technical support.

stakingBlock.description: Dash is not a Proof of Stake protocol, but it pays part of the block reward to masternodes to perform certain work for the network. Thanks to this, some popular staking services also work with Dash. You can deposit your Dash in any one of these staking services and obtain a return in exchange for the work your coins will do for the network through these services. If you have 1,000 Dash or more, you may also want to consider starting a masternode instead and work for the network directly.

defi.title: DeFi
defi.description: DeFi, or Decentralized Finance, offers a way to participate in financial services without a centralized intermediary. Dash is available in a growing number of DeFi platforms.

custodyBlock.title:
Custody Solutions
for Peace of Mind
custodyBlock.description: BitGo and CYBAVO provide best-in-class custody and multi-sig security solutions for Dash. Whether you are a business, fund, or high-net-worth individual, these providers offer institutional-grade asset protection.

bitgo.name: BitGo
bitgo.description: BitGo provides a simple and secure REST API to integrate multi-signature wallets with support for Dash's InstantSend. Multi-Sig HD Wallets enable enterprise-grade security.

cybavo.name: CYBAVO
cybavo.description: CYBAVO provides an enterprise wallet and custody platform for digital assets, helping businesses securely manage and transfer cryptocurrency.

accountingBlock.title: Accounting & Tax
accountingBlock.description: Some of the best-known names in cryptocurrency accounting and tax services work with Dash. They provide cost-effective and easy to use platforms to comply with local tax reporting requirements.

hero.title: Regulatory Information
hero.subtitle: Dash is not a security and offers greater transparency and less risk than Bitcoin with regards to privacy. Learn more about how legal regulations apply to Dash.

fincen.title:
DCG response
to FinCEN
fincen.description: Dash Core Group supplements the original Financial Crimes Enforcement Network ('FinCEN') with this additional information with respect to the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, published on December 23, 2020, titled, 'Requirements for Certain Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currency or Digital Assets'.

fatf.title:
Dash Complies with
the FATF Rule
fatf.description: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) released their guidelines for countries' regulations of the cryptocurrency industry in 2019, including the Travel Rule. Dash is in full compliance with the FATF guidelines. For more information, please contact us at

security.title: Dash is Not a Security
security.description: The status of Dash as "not a security" has been validated by many entities, most recently the Crypto Rating Council which provided the best possible score of 1.0, equivalent to the score for Bitcoin. The score takes into account various points within the Howey Test to conclude that Dash has few characteristics that are consistent with being a security.
security.secondParagraph: Business compliance officers and regulators interested in speaking with Dash Core Group and/or requesting our legal opinions on the matter, please reach out to us at

kycamlBlock.title: KYC/AML Services
kycamlBlock.description: Day-to-day compliance requirements can be difficult to scale for many businesses within the cryptocurrency industry, such as KYC/AML compliance for exchanges. The largest names in KYC/AML for cryptocurrency help ensure that businesses remain in compliance. Our partners in this space provide state of the art KYC/AML services to some of the best known cryptocurrency companies, law enforcement agencies, and financial institutions around the globe.

blockchainIntel.name:
Blockchain
Intel
blockchainIntel.description: BlockchainIntel offers a REST API that provides a risk score and corresponding reasons for blockchain wallet addresses. The score is based on known profiles tied to the address owner and behavioral data such as geographic location, links to fraud, scams and known merchants.

chainalysis.name: Chainalysis
chainalysis.description: Chainalysis works to create transparency for a global economy built on blockchains, enabling banks, business, and governments to have a common understanding of how people use cryptocurrency.

hero.title: Providers and Tools
hero.description:
The following providers offer a range of options that vary in terms of development effort required. Payment Processors provide a simple and quick way to begin accepting payments without any development skill required.

Custody and API Providers enable blockchain interactions typically used by larger merchants and service providers.

anypay.name: Anypay
anypay.description: Anypay eCommerce, Point-of-Sale, Web & Mobile, APIs Anypay is an easy-to-use, multi-coin payment processor helping businesses accept Dash since 2016. A fully open-source suite of tools offers e-commerce plugins, POS integrations, web & mobile apps, and APIs for developers.

btcpay.name: BTCPay Server
btcpay.description: BTCPay Server is a free, self-hosted and fully open-source cryptocurrency payment processor designed with security, privacy and censorship-resistance at its core.

coinpayments.name: CoinPayments
coinpayments.description: CoinPayments is an integrated payment gateway with a wide range of plugins available for popular webcarts.

coinspaid.name: Coinspaid
coinspaid.description: Coinspaid offers a white label backoffice payments solution with on-the-fly Fiat (EUR) conversion and instant transaction confirmations.

ankerpay.name: AnkerPay
ankerpay.description: AnkerPay POS is a crypto payment processor that allows merchants to accept crypto currencies and receive settlement in the local currency.

nowpayments.name: NOWPayments
nowpayments.description: NOWPayments allows everyone to accept crypto payments on their websites, online stores, and social media accounts. It's a non-custodial service and supports more than 50 cryptocurrencies.

custodyProviders.chip: "Cloud Infrastructure" Providers Enable Direct Access to the Blockchain
custodyProviders.title: Custody Solutions and API Providers

bitgo.name: BitGo
bitgo.description: BitGo provides a simple and robust REST API and client SDK to integrate digital currency wallets with your application. InstantSend is fully supported. Features: Multi-Signature HD Wallets, Custody Solutions and Wallet Operations.

blockcypher.name: BlockCypher
blockcypher.description: BlockCypher is a non-custodial, REST API and client SDK for interacting with blockchains. Features: Transaction Building, Address Generation, Event Notifications, Payment Forwarding.

lukka.name: Lukka
lukka.description: Lukka's blockchain agnostic AML Platform uses proprietary algorithms to provide structured, actionable data that solves compliance and transaction risk issues for blockchain and cryptocurrencies. Features: Anti-money laundering (AML) solution, Know Your Customer (KYC) services, Blockchain Analytics, Register/ Authenticate digital assets, Track/Monitor source of crypto funds.

cybavo.name: CYBAVO
cybavo.description: CYBAVO provides a turn-key, enterprise-level wallet and custody platform, offering fully customizable policies, segregated roles and multi-level approval chains. Features: Enterprise Wallets, Custody Solutions and Mobile Wallet SDK.

nownodes.name: NOWNodes
nownodes.description: NOWNodes is an explorer and node API provider. It is meant for start-up entrepreneurs and crypto enthusiasts who would like to gain access to major blockchain networks without needing to establish their own nodes. Features: Explorer and Node API, WebSocket API, Powerful Servers (1GB/s), SLA, Backup Solution.

getblock.name: GetBlock
getblock.description: GetBlock offers blockchain developers fast and easy access to Dash nodes and other popular cryptocurrencies over the JSON-RPC, REST, and WebSocket protocols. Features: JSON-RPC, REST API and WebSocket APIs.

sdks.chip: The Following Resources are Used to Build Custom Integrations
sdks.title: Software Development Kits and Tools

nodejs.name: NodeJS
nodejs.description: Dashcore-Lib is a library for working with the Dash Protocol in client-side "Browserified" (JavaScript) settings as well as in server-side (NodeJS) applications. Insight API utilizes this open-source framework as part of a full-stack implementation.

java.name: Java
java.description: DashJ is a library for working with the Dash protocol in Java or JVM environment. It can be used for a variety of wallet functions including InstantSend. This library also includes an SPV implementation which allows for transaction verification in mobile applications.

dotnet.name: .NET
dotnet.description: NBitcoin is the most complete cryptocurrency library for the .NET platform and includes support for Dash. It implements all most relevant Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs) and Dash Improvement Proposals (DIPs) and provides low level access to Dash primitives.

python.name: Python
python.description: PyCoin is an implementation of utility routines that are useful when working with the Dash Protocol. It is frequently used alongside Python-DashRPC and has been tested with Python 2.7, 3.6 and 3.7.

bugBounty.title: Bug Bounty Program
bugBounty.description: The Dash Core Group Bug Bounty Program allows developers to discover and resolve bugs before the general public is aware of such bugs, preventing incidents of widespread abuse.
